text:
anya: quick question — we need to roll vpc-private-config v2 to private customers this week. plan is a staggered canary (5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%) but a lot of these targets are air-gapped or using long-polling agents. how do we handle control-plane pushes vs offline bundles? and what guards should the console expose?

matt: +1 to staggered ramp. for VPC (non-airgapped) control-plane push + agents that poll every 30–60s works. problem is customers with strict egress or offline hosts — they won't see pushed updates.

manual off-line path: build signed bundle (tar.gz) + manifest with checksum; customers can import via console or support upload. we should avoid forcing a single flow.

lee: recommendation: treat rollout as two coordinated artifacts: a control-plane rollout (routing/weights) and a config bundle release (model/kv/cache config). they have independent propagation semantics. console UX must show both statuses separately per-customer.

ivana: for SRE guards: we need automatic rollback if telemetry crosses thresholds. proposed quick rules: if error_rate > 1% absolute or p95 latency increases > 30% over baseline within a 10m window, block further ramps and roll back canary. also require checksum validation on agent side or we risk partial-config state.

zach: for air-gapped customers we also need to track "last-seen-manifest" timestamp and report stale warnings. otherwise ops will think a rollout finished when it didn't. console should show: manifest_version, manifest_checksum, last_seen_ts, propagation_state.

anya: good — what about the ramp timing? some customers are very sensitive; a single 15m interval might be too quick if propagation is slow. suggestion: default ramp: 5% -> wait for stable 30m -> 20% -> wait 30m -> 50% -> wait 30m -> 100% and allow per-customer overrides.

matt: agree. also implement a per-customer propagation window for control-plane updates. if control-plane push returns 202 accepted but agent hasn't polled in X minutes, mark as PENDING rather than SUCCESS. X should default to 10m but be configurable per-deployment.

lee: infra note — agents have exponential backoff on fail, and for air-gapped installs we support manual bundle apply. we need a way to mark a customer as "requires-bundle" so their rollout path is bundle-based automatically. that avoids human error.

ivana: telemetry hooks: we need per-route and per-customer metrics. do not rely solely on global aggregates. a bad config for one VPC can be invisible in global metrics. console should surface per-route 5xxs, token errors, and request distribution.

deploy-bot: Deploy started -> manifest:v2 -> target_group:vpc-canary -> traffic:5% :rocket: 

zach: edge case — control-plane TLS cert rotation can delay agent polls if cert chains mismatch. we should fail-safe the rollout: if agent reports cert error or manifest signature mismatch, mark it FAILED and notify customer + SE team.

anya: what about guards for config schema mismatches? we had one incident where a missing field caused silent fallback behavior.

matt: validate manifest against schema pre-push and add preflight checks: schema, checksum, semantic diff (breaking-change hints). console should show preflight status and block rollout if "fatal" errors present. non-fatal warnings can be acknowledged by user.

lee: example rollout policy (we can iterate on UX):
```
rollout_policy: 
  name: vpc-staggered-canary
  stages:
    - name: canary
      split: 5
      metrics:
        - name: error_rate
          threshold: 0.01
        - name: latency_p95
          threshold_pct: 30
      interval: 30m
    - name: ramp
      split: [20,50,100]
      interval: 30m
  propagation_window: 10m  # control-plane visibility window for agent poll
```

ivana: add an automatic "circuit-breaker" action: on breach -> cut traffic to 0 for that customer, flag manifest as bad, and optionally deploy previous manifest. must be executable by automation or a single-click rollback in console.

anya: can we show per-customer estimated time-to-complete based on last_seen_ts + propagation_window and queued ramp steps? that would help PMs/sales set expectations.

zach: we can approximate based on agent heartbeat and current stage. for air-gapped flagged customers, show "manual bundle required" and a link to create a bundle download.

matt: one more: expose a "dry-run" where control-plane validates routing decisions without switching traffic, and agents validate bundle download/validation in background (if they can). helpful for staging.

ivana: also we should log a full audit trail: who triggered rollout, who acknowledged warnings, timestamps for each stage per-customer. compliance asks for that.

anya: ok actionable items: 1) console: separate control-plane vs bundle propagation view + per-customer last_seen_ts and propagation_state. 2) eng-runtime: implement propagation_window and per-customer routing path with requires-bundle flag. 3) eng-sre: define default guard thresholds and circuit-breaker action. 4) devex: UI for bundle creation/download + dry-run. i'll consolidate into a spec.

matt: sounds good. i'll prototype the manifest state machine and a small API that returns per-customer propagation status.

lee: i'll add the propagation_window config and backoff visibility hooks in the agent telemetry.

ivana: i'll draft the SRE runbook for rollback, thresholds, and checklist for handling air-gapped failures.

deploy-bot: Canary metrics stream attached: http://internal.metrics/redwood/canary/manifest-v2 (updates every 60s)

anya: thanks everyone. i'll post the spec PR later today and tag y'all. :thumbsup:
